task.description:
Hard-gate CODE-DESIGNER's two ISS-0439 design-exploration artefacts (Step 1's handoff, listed in artifacts_in) against ISS-0439's own six acceptance criteria (docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml). This is NOT an implementation-readiness gate (there is no implementation for this issue) -- gate for completeness and accuracy of the exploration and decision record instead. Concretely:

1. Read docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml in full for the six ACs.
2. Read both produced artefacts in full: lib/letflow/design/iss0439-1c-taxonomy-mapping.md and docs/migration/decisions/0019-defer-1c-typed-templates.md.
3. Independently verify, not trust, CODE-DESIGNER's factual claims against the actual current code and docs/requirements.yaml -- specifically: (a) that lib/letflow/event_store/instance_projection.ex is genuinely the projection module referenced (open it and confirm the moduledoc claim about being 'rebuildable from a fold over events'); (b) that lib/letflow/repository/artifact_kind.ex genuinely has no :entity value in its atom list yet; (c) that REQ-225 through REQ-231 in docs/requirements.yaml are genuinely all status: pending as claimed in both artefacts (re-check yourself, do not copy the table); (d) that 0019 was genuinely the next free decision-record number at write time (list docs/migration/decisions/ yourself).
4. Confirm neither artefact contains a fenced code block of Elixir/Ecto/JSON-schema (grep for triple-backtick fences yourself).
5. Confirm neither artefact creates or references creating a docs/requirements.yaml entry, a schema, or implementation code.
6. Confirm AC6 is genuinely satisfied: the artefacts state a real verdict (see the taxonomy-mapping artefact's section 4) rather than avoiding a position.
7. Confirm AC1/AC2 are satisfied: the decision record states the three reasons and cross-references the mapping artefact, and the mapping artefact grounds each of Directory/Document/Register/Report against a real, named, actually-read module.

This run is deliberately NOT running WF-02's usual 'is this design implementable' checks (no ELIXIR-DEV/FRONTEND-DEV will ever receive this design) -- the bar is factual grounding and AC coverage, not buildability.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of ISS-0439's six acceptance_criteria (docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml) is checked individually against the two artefacts, with a PASS/FAIL verdict per criterion stated in result.summary -- not a single overall impression
At least two of CODE-DESIGNER's factual claims are independently re-verified against the actual source (not copied from the artefact's own citations) and the verification method is stated
Confirms zero fenced code blocks in either artefact via an actual grep, not a visual skim
If any criterion is unmet, FAIL names the specific gap and which artefact/section it is in

result.summary: Per-criterion verdicts against ISS-0439's six acceptance_criteria (docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml): AC1 (deferral + 3 reasons recorded under docs/migration/decisions/) PASS -- 0019-defer-1c-typed-templates.md exists, states all three reasons in weight order, quoted verbatim from the filing. AC2 (review triggers stated explicitly) PASS -- 0019's 'Review triggers' section names exactly three: concrete tenant/domain, observed cross-tenant duplication, ERP-adjacent market decision. AC3 (1C taxonomy mapped onto existing machinery) PASS -- iss0439-1c-taxonomy-mapping.md SS1.1-1.4/SS2 ground each of Directory/Document/Register/Report against real, named, actually-read modules. AC4 (dependency on ISS-0438/queue task 438 stated) PASS -- both artefacts state no typed-template design proceeds until REQ-225..231 reach done, not merely scoped. AC5 (no requirements/schema/code created) PASS -- zero fenced code blocks in either file (grepped both directly, 0 matches each), no docs/requirements.yaml edits, no schema files. AC6 (real verdict recorded, not a silent close or a hedge) PASS -- mapping artefact SS4 gives a plain verdict: not recommended for adoption now, not rejected outright, with mechanism-grounded reasoning. Independent re-verification performed (not copied from the artefacts' own citations): (a) read lib/letflow/event_store/instance_projection.ex directly -- confirmed it is the real projection module and its moduledoc (lines 74-76) states 'this is a projection table: rebuildable at any time from a fold over events', matching the artefact's quote. (b) read lib/letflow/repository/artifact_kind.ex directly -- confirmed @artifact_kinds is exactly [:definition, :form, :schema, :service_catalog, :script, :module, :scenario], no :entity value, matching the claim. (c) grepped docs/requirements.yaml for 'id: REQ-22[5-9]|id: REQ-23[01]' with context and confirmed each of REQ-225..REQ-231 is immediately followed by 'status: pending' -- re-derived myself, not copied from either artefact's table. (d) ran `ls docs/migration/decisions/` directly -- confirmed 0001 through 0018 exist and 0019 was genuinely the next free number at write time. Grepped both artefacts for triple-backtick fences via the Grep tool (not a visual skim): 0 matches in lib/letflow/design/iss0439-1c-taxonomy-mapping.md, 0 matches in docs/migration/decisions/0019-defer-1c-typed-templates.md. No gaps found; both artefacts are factually grounded and cover all six ACs.
